cues.en: Instructor: I know you've heard me say before that I'm really excited about doing some certain video, but this time it is true.

cues.en: Okay, then let's see.
We'll just plot this so you can see what it looks like.
So here's what the data looked like in the data space.
cues.zh: 這是資料空間中的資料。

cues.en: So I've just created this disc and then rotated it by Pi over four by 45 degrees.

cues.en: And here we have our data.

cues.en: So we can already tell what those are gonna look like.
The first principle component is gonna be along this direction here.

cues.en: And then, so we get the coefficients, which I will interpret those later on.
So I'll these turn out to be the eigen values.
We'll work with them later.
And the principle component scores, and this is the thing that we are interested in.
cues.zh: 以及我們關心的主成分分數。

cues.en: This is gonna be how we get the data in the PC space.
cues.zh: 藉此取得主成分空間中的資料。

cues.en: So here you see what the data looked like in the PC space.
cues.zh: 這是 PC 空間的樣子。

cues.en: And again, this is just a pure rotation of these data.
So we've just spun around on the axis.
You can see these three data points here and then one.

cues.zh: 這就是如何實作投影片內容。

So we're gonna read this in and then visualize what is going on with these data.
cues.zh: 讀進來、視覺化，看看資料怎麼回事。

cues.en: So when we look at this variable, we see that it is 29,000 by 12, and this corresponds to 29,000 different events.
And each event is 12-time points long.
cues.zh: 每個事件長 12 個時間點。

cues.en: So here you see the average, this is just the averaging over all these events.
It goes a little bit down and then up and then down again.
And here you see an image.
So these are all 29,000 events, and then they're over time here.
So this is just the average of all of these guys here.
So, what are we looking at here?
Well, these spikes come from action potentials of individual neurons.
cues.zh: 這些脈衝來自個別神經元的動作電位。

cues.en: A neuron is a brain cell.
And so when brain cells become excited, then they activate, they emit an action potential, which is like this jolt
cues.zh: 腦細胞興奮後，活化、發出動作電位，就是一股

cues.en: of electrochemical energy and it's commonly called a spike.
Now the thing is, when you lower an electrode, which is like a very small antenna into the brain, this is not done in humans.
cues.zh: 把像微小天線的電極插入大腦時，這不是在人類身上做。

cues.en: This is done in small animals like mice for example.
When you lower a tiny electrode into the brain, it doesn't only record from one single brain cell, it can record that one electrode can record from multiple
cues.zh: 微小電極不只記錄單一腦細胞，同一電極可以同時記錄多個

cues.en: brain cells at the same time.
Now typically you're likely to get one or two, sometimes three different brain cells that are all recorded on the same electrode.
cues.zh: 通常一、兩個，有時三個細胞，共用同一電極記錄。

cues.en: So how can we tell which wave forms which events in this matrix come from, which neuron?
cues.zh: 如何知道矩陣中哪些波形、事件，來自哪個神經元？

cues.en: So, that's what we're going to do here.
We're gonna use PCA to help us visualize this data to see what is actually happening in the data space.
cues.zh: 用 PCA 幫助視覺化，了解資料空間發生什麼。

cues.en: Okay, so there we go.
Now we run PCA, and this is basically the same as I showed above, but I'm also getting out this additional variable here, which is called explVar.
cues.zh: 執行 PCA，基本上同上，但多取一個 explVar 變數。

cues.en: So, that's the explained variance.
This is the eigen values and they're converted into percent of variance explained.
cues.zh: 特徵值轉成解釋變異百分比。

cues.en: So let's see.
Let's run all of this.
Actually, let me start off just by running this code up here.

This is just like what I showed you in the slides.

cues.zh: 第一個成分解釋 50% 變異。

cues.en: And then the next component explains around like 18% of the variance or so.

We can also take the cumulative sum of the explained variances, and that's just a different way of looking at the same data.
cues.zh: 也能取解釋變異的累積和，是同資料的另一種看法。

cues.en: So it looks like there are two components that are accounting for a lot of the data.
cues.zh: 似乎兩個成分解釋很多資料。

cues.en: And then as we add more and more of these components, we are accounting for more and more of the data, but not that much.
cues.zh: 再加成分，解釋更多，但幅度不大。

cues.en: It's less and less of the data are being accounted for by adding more principle components.
cues.zh: 新增主成分所解釋的資料愈來愈少。

cues.en: Okay, so now we can look at the principle component weights.
Now it's a little bit weird to think about here because these are actually the way that the axes in the 12-dimensional space are being
cues.zh: 這有點難想像，因為它們其實是十二維空間座標軸，

cues.zh: 為最佳主成分而旋轉的方式。

cues.en: So it looks like a time course here, I'm plotting them as a time course, but in fact these are rotation vectors.
cues.zh: 我畫成時間歷程，看似時間歷程，其實是旋轉向量。

cues.en: These are ways of rotating the original data space into this optimized PC space where we're just looking at these two components here.
cues.zh: 把原始空間轉到最佳 PC 空間，這裡只看兩個成分。

cues.en: Okay, so now we're gonna plot the PC scores.
Now remember, this was the original data space.
This was the PC space for this simple dataset.
cues.zh: 這是簡單資料的 PC 空間。

cues.en: In this particular case, we're not doing any dimension reduction because the data already started off being two dimensional.
cues.zh: 那個例子沒有降維，因為原本就是二維。

cues.en: But now with these spikes, the data are 12-dimensional, these are time points, but each time point is a dimension of the data.
cues.zh: 但脈衝資料十二維，雖然是時間點，但每點是資料的一個維度。

cues.en: So we have 12-dimensional data, we cannot visualize that.

cues.zh: 所以忽略其他維度，進行降維、壓縮。

cues.en: So we're ignoring dimensions three through 12, and we're just going to look at the data along the first two dimensions, and that's what we will see here.
cues.zh: 忽略第 3 到 12 維，只看前兩維，就會看到這裡。

cues.en: Okay, so here is principle component one and principle component two.
And each dot here corresponds to a different spike.
So there's going to be, how many of these things are there?
29,000 dots in this space.
Now what's really remarkable is you look at this and what do you see?
What do you see here in this plot?
Right, you see clusters, you see two big clusters.
These are separable clusters.
Here's one cluster and here is another cluster.
So this tells us that this one electrode, this one tiny wire was actually recording spikes action potentials from two different brain cells.
cues.zh: 表示這一條小電極，記錄到兩個不同腦細胞的脈衝、動作電位。

cues.en: Those two brain cells happened to be physically close to each other and therefore physically close to the wire.
cues.zh: 兩細胞彼此靠近，也靠近導線。

cues.en: And that's why we were able to record both of those.

cues.zh: 這張圖看不到兩種脈衝，但某些波形，

cues.en: some of the rows in this matrix come from spike one, and some of them come from spike two.
cues.zh: 矩陣某些列，來自第一種脈衝，其他來自第二種。

cues.en: So, what we can do, so this is a pretty standard neuroscience technique now, is to basically look at these data, apply some kind of clustering algorithm to say
cues.zh: 這是相當標準的神經科學技術，查看資料、套某種分群演算法，判定

cues.en: that you know, these spikes.
So, all these dots, these come from neuron one, and these dots come from neuron two.
cues.zh: 這些點來自神經元一，那些來自神經元二。

cues.en: And remember, each one of these dots corresponds to a different row in this matrix.
cues.zh: 記住，每點對應矩陣不同列。

cues.en: Okay so, I'm sure you're thinking that the next step is going to be to run K-means clustering on this.
cues.zh: 你一定想到，下一步做 K-means。

cues.zh: 這裡不做，下一支無監督學習挑戰，由你完成。

cues.en: Okay so, in addition to the standard numpy and matplotlib, which we probably used on literally every single code here, I think.
cues.zh: 除了大概每份程式都用的 NumPy 與 Matplotlib，

cues.en: Anyway, we're also using the PCA function from psychic learn.
So we start by creating the data, and these are going to be two dimensional data, and I'm creating these as a disc.
cues.zh: 先建立二維資料，做成盤狀。

cues.en: And then I'm gonna rotate that disc to create correlated data.
So it's a thousand data points.
And you can see here are the X values and the Y values.
And the X values are not variance scaled here.
These are just normally distributed random numbers, so variants of one, and the Y coordinates are standard deviation scaled by 0.4.
cues.zh: 只是常態隨機數，變異數 1；Y 則乘標準差尺度 0.4。

cues.zh: 所以 X 軸寬，Y 軸窄；抱歉，是 X 寬，Y 窄。

cues.en: And then what I do is come up with this rotation matrix.
So this is something from trigonometry or geometry and orthogonal rotation matrix.
cues.zh: 三角學或幾何中的正交旋轉矩陣。

cues.en: And then I just rotate the data by Pi over four, and you'll see what effect that has on the results that basically creates this correlated data set like this.
cues.zh: 把資料轉 π/4，效果就是這樣的相關資料。

cues.en: So this is another way to create correlated multi-variate data sets.
cues.zh: 是建立多變量相關資料的另一方法。

cues.en: Okay so, you can already guess what the principle components analysis is going to look like here, because this is really similar to the example that I showed in the slides.

cues.en: So the first principle component, we expect to look like this.
And the second principle component, we expect to look like this.

cues.en: of the principle components analysis to the data, and that gives us our PC scores.
cues.zh: 套到資料，取得 PC 分數。

cues.en: So the PC scores are basically the data transformed into the PC space.
cues.zh: 就是轉到 PC 空間的資料。

cues.en: So let's make a plot of this and see what they look like.
So here we see the data space, and here you see the principle component space.
cues.zh: 這是資料空間，這是主成分空間。

cues.en: That's small typo there.
My apologies, that should say PC space there.
Okay, so we've taken these data and we've just rotated them` so that the PC one axis, this X axis now contains most
cues.zh: 旋轉資料，讓 PC1 這條 X 軸包含大部分

cues.zh: 只是示範如何用程式做到。

So the data set is around 29,000 events and 12 features.
So those features are actually time points, and we can average all of these data together.
cues.zh: 特徵其實是時間點，能把資料全部平均。

cues.en: So each row is a separate event, a separate observation, and so we can average them all together.

cues.en: And that looks like this.
You can see it goes down and then up, and then it goes down again.
So this is called a spike or an action potential.
So these data come from a brain.
So the brain contains a lot of cells, these are called neurons.
cues.zh: 腦有很多細胞，叫神經元。

cues.en: And neurons work by getting excited from other neurons.
cues.zh: 靠其他神經元讓它興奮而運作。

cues.en: And when a neuron gets enough excitation, it will emit this jolt of electrochemical energy, which is called an action potential.
cues.zh: 興奮足夠，就放出一股電化學能量，動作電位。

cues.en: And colloquially we call it a spike.
So the neuron is spiking.

cues.zh: 量測方式是用很細、很小的導線插入大腦。

cues.zh: 電極同時量測全部細胞活動，都放同一資料集。

cues.en: So the question is whether we can use something like principle components analysis to help us understand what we have in our data, okay?
cues.zh: 問題是，能否用 PCA 了解資料裡有什麼。

cues.en: And that's the idea.
We're gonna apply basically the same code as above to do a PCA of this spikes matrix.
cues.zh: 用基本上與上面相同程式，對 spikes 矩陣做 PCA。

cues.en: So over in here in this plot, we're looking at a cumulative sum of this percent variance accounted for here.
cues.zh: 這張是這些百分比的累積和。

cues.en: So basically what we see is that as you add more and more components, of course you're explaining more and more of the data.
cues.zh: 加更多成分，當然解釋更多資料。

cues.en: This is analogous to how in a regression model, as you add more and more independent variables, you're going to account for more and more variants in the signal.

The first two components.

What's going on in here?

There's two clusters.
Here's one big cluster and another big cluster.

cues.zh: 對腦科學家來說，表示這條電極記錄到兩個不同神經元。
